Buzz の huddle（Slack のハドル相当）の構成も調べた。結論: WebRTC/SFU/LiveKit は使わず、リレー内蔵の独自ボイス。

■ 部屋 = NIP-29 の一時チャンネル
huddle の部屋は TTL 付きの NIP-29 グループ（metadata に ttl / ttl_deadline）。通常のチャンネルと同じ枠組みで、期限切れで消える。

■ トランスポート = 専用 WebSocket（非 WebRTC）
音声はリレーの専用エンドポイント wss://<relay>/huddle/{channel_id}/audio に流す。
接続時に challenge/response で鍵署名認証してから開始（NIP-42 的）。

■ 中継 = リレー内蔵のオーディオ mesh
サーバ側 crates/buzz-relay/src/audio（room / mesh / handler）が参加者間で音声フレームを中継。SFU/mesh をリレー自身に内蔵している。

■ コーデック = Opus / 48kHz
クライアント（Tauri/Rust）は opus クレートで Opus/48kHz。
独自バイナリ wire（v2, 8byte ヘッダ: seq / ts_48k / level_dbov / flags、DTX=無音時送信抑制）。
rubato でリサンプル、rodio で再生、jitter buffer + playout をクライアント処理。
https://opus-codec.org

■ AI エージェント参加（最大20）
huddle にエージェントが最大20参加可能（MAX_HUDDLE_AGENTS=20）。
クライアントに STT / TTS / transcription パイプラインがあり、聞く・喋る。
音声エンジンは Kyutai の Mimi neural codec（24kHz）。※人間同士の Opus 経路とは別系統。
https://github.com/kyutai-labs/moshi

Buzz の設計まとめ（algia で一通り触ってみた）

Buzz は Block 製のセルフホスト型チームワークスペースで、Slack 的なチャンネルを Nostr プロトコル上に実装している。
repo: https://github.com/block/buzz

■ プロトコル基盤: NIP-29（relay-based groups）
チャンネル = NIP-29 のグループ。
- チャンネル投稿 = kind:9 に h タグ（グループID）
- グループ metadata = kind:39000（d=グループID, name/about/public|private）、管理者 39001 / メンバー 39002
- 参加/退出 = kind:9021 / 9022、削除（モデレーション）= kind:9005（e タグは1件のみ）
- リアクションも kind:7 に h タグ
https://github.com/nostr-protocol/nips/blob/master/29.md

■ 認証: NIP-42（必須）
未認証で subscribe すると CLOSED ではなく NOTICE（auth-required）で弾かれる。接続直後の AUTH challenge に対する先行認証（kind:22242）が要る。HTTP 側は NIP-98。
https://github.com/nostr-protocol/nips/blob/master/42.md

■ メディア: Blossom 互換を内蔵
リレーに Blossom 互換のメディアサーバを内蔵。/media にマウントされ URL は content-addressable（sha256+拡張子）。
- upload: PUT /media/upload（Blossom kind:24242 auth + X-SHA-256 ヘッダ、BUD-11、50MB、要メンバー）
- get: GET /media/{sha256}.{ext}（要認証）
- 実体は MinIO（S3互換）
例: https://vim-jp.communities.buzz.xyz/media/<sha256>.png
https://github.com/hzrd149/blossom

■ リレー実装
strfry / relay29 / nostr-rs-relay 等の既存単体リレーではなく Buzz 専用実装。
- Rust モノレポ、Axum(WebSocket) + Tokio
- event store: PostgreSQL（created_at で月次パーティション）
- pub/sub・presence・typing: Redis
- media: MinIO
- crates: buzz-core / buzz-db / buzz-auth(NIP-42/98) / buzz-pubsub / buzz-search(Postgres FTS) / buzz-audit / buzz-workflow / buzz-relay

■ 対応 NIP（NIP-11 より）
1,2,10,11,16,17,23,25,29,33,38,42,50,56,43
※ NIP-18（リポスト）は非対応。

# NOT A MEETUP 2026/08/14

Nostr Night for English Speakers in Japan
This is not a meetup. It’s only freedom.

An English-language night in Yotsuya, Tokyo, exploring Nostr, Bitcoin, privacy, open protocols, cypherpunk culture, and individual freedom.

The entire event—including the talks and networking—will be conducted in English.

You do not need to be a native or fluent English speaker. Anyone interested in discussing technology and culture in English, or connecting with Tokyo’s international community, is welcome.

# ABOUT
In the mid-2010s, Tokyo was home to one of the world’s most active international Bitcoin communities.

Developers, entrepreneurs, hackers, and early adopters gathered every week. Some participants went on to lead major global companies and projects, while others built infrastructure that remains important to Bitcoin today. For better or worse, with events including the rise and collapse of Mt. Gox, Tokyo became one of the key cities in Bitcoin’s early history.

NOT A MEETUP is an attempt to bring that energy back—reimagined for Tokyo in the 2020s.

Today, powerful technology companies are becoming increasingly intertwined with governments, finance, and surveillance infrastructure. Technology that was once expected to liberate individuals is often used instead to strengthen large platforms and institutions.

Open and decentralized technologies such as Bitcoin and Nostr point in another direction.

This event is not only about introducing new technology. It is about returning power to individuals—and exploring the ideas, music, art, and independent culture surrounding that goal.

After the talks, the night continues with music, drinks, and open networking.

# PROGRAM
Times and session lengths may change.
 All sessions will be presented in English.

## 8:00 PM — OPENING TRANSMISSION
A short introduction to the background of NOT A MEETUP and the international community we hope to build from Tokyo.

## 8:05 PM — NOT A MEETUP
Justin_Tokyo ⚡️ 
Why We Are Not Building Another Institution

5–10 minutes

Justin will introduce the philosophy behind the event.

What would a community look like if it belonged to the individuals participating in it—not to a company, platform, or institution?

A short keynote exploring permissionless communities and how technology and culture can support individual freedom.

## 8:15 PM — BUZZ: THE POST-SLACK WORKSPACE
nostr: 
Nostr, AI Agents and the Future of Collaboration

15 minutes

Recently introduced by Jack Dorsey, Buzz is a Nostr-based next-generation workspace where humans and AI agents can collaborate within the same channels and projects.

Kohei was a speaker at Nostrasia 2023, where Jack Dorsey also appeared, and has deep technical knowledge of Nostr and its ecosystem.

Using Buzz as a case study, this session will explore how Nostr may expand beyond social media, how humans and AI agents could collaborate through open protocols, and what it might mean to reduce our dependence on centralized workplace platforms.

## 8:30 PM — NOSTR.BUILD
The Fishcake (nostr.build) 
Building Media Infrastructure for an Open Network

10–15 minutes

nostr.build is a media-hosting service for images, video, audio, and other content used across the Nostr ecosystem.

fishcake, the developer behind nostr.build, will discuss the problems the service was created to solve, its integration with Nostr clients, privacy-conscious media delivery, and the practical experience of building and operating infrastructure for an open network.

## 8:45 PM — MUSIC, DRINKS & OPEN NETWORKING
After the talks, the night continues with music, drinks, and open networking.

Meet Nostr users, Bitcoiners, developers, AI builders, artists, founders, cypherpunks, and others interested in technology and individual freedom.

Alcoholic and non-alcoholic drinks will be available.

That's why it's not possible to `git pull` from the GRASP servers after new changes arrive (I got `fatal: refusing to merge unrelated histories`).

Here's the full history from GH:

```
$ git clone https://github.com/arbadacarbaYK/gittr.git
$ cd gittr && git rev-list --count HEAD
1072
```

And here's the single commit from GRASP:

```
$ git clone nostr://npub1n2ph08n4pqz4d3jk6n2p35p2f4ldhc5g5tu7dhftfpueajf4rpxqfjhzmc/gittr
$ # or git clone https://git.gittr.space/npub1n2ph08n4pqz4d3jk6n2p35p2f4ldhc5g5tu7dhftfpueajf4rpxqfjhzmc/gittr.git
$ cd gittr && git rev-list --count HEAD
1
```

```

405
```
